title: 1 · Hangul in one sitting
blurb: The alphabet: 14 consonants, 10 vowels, how blocks stack.

title: 2 · Politeness levels
blurb: Why every verb has two endings, and which one to use.

title: 3 · Meeting people
blurb: Introduce yourself, ask the four standard questions, say goodbye correctly.

title: 4 · Sound changes: why 감사합니다 sounds different
blurb: Four habits that make spoken Korean differ from its spelling. Learn to expect them.

title: 5 · Nouns and 은/는
blurb: Names of things, this/that, 이에요/예요, and the topic marker 은/는.

title: 6 · 있어요 and 없어요
blurb: There is / there isn't, have / don't have, the subject marker 이/가, and where things are with 에.

title: 7 · Pronouns and question words
blurb: I, we, this, that, here, there, and the seven question words that unlock real conversations.

title: 8 · Verbs
blurb: Every verb ends in 다, never changes for I/you/she, and adjectives are verbs too.

title: 9 · Present tense: the 요-form
blurb: Turn any dictionary verb into the polite present: 아요, 어요 or 해요.

title: 10 · Past tense: 았어요 / 었어요
blurb: Take the 요-form, swap 요 for ㅆ어요, and you are talking about yesterday.

title: 11 · Future and plans: -(으)ㄹ 거예요
blurb: Say what you will do, and guess what will probably happen.

title: 12 · Word order and 을/를
blurb: Subject · Object · Verb, the object marker 을/를, and when it drops.

title: 13 · 에 and 에서, plus the particle map
blurb: 에 for where you go, where things are and when; 에서 for where you do things and where you come from.

title: 14 · Saying no: 안 and -지 않아요
blurb: 안 + verb, 공부 안 해요, -지 않아요, 아니에요 for nouns, and 없어요.

title: 15 · 도 and 만: also and only
blurb: 도 (also, too) and 만 (only) replace 은/는, 이/가, 을/를 but stack after 에 and 에서.

title: 16 · Putting nouns and verbs together
blurb: Four sentence shapes that cover most of what you'll say, then how to grow them.

title: 17 · Want and like: -고 싶어요, 좋아해요
blurb: Say what you want to do and what you like. Two patterns you will use every day.

title: 18 · Two number systems
blurb: Native for counting and age, Sino-Korean for money and time.

title: 19 · Eating out
blurb: Ordering, counters, and the two meal phrases everyone says.

title: 20 · Getting around
blurb: Asking where, understanding the answer, taxis and subway.

title: 21 · Titles & honorifics
blurb: 씨, 님, 오빠/언니 — what to call people and when a bare name is rude.

title: 22 · Making plans
blurb: Suggest, invite, agree: ㄹ까요 / ㄹ래요 / 자, and 같이.

title: 23 · Texting like a local
blurb: ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, dropped particles, and the shorthand everyone uses on KakaoTalk.

title: 24 · Counters
blurb: You can't say 'two coffees' without one. The ten counters that cover daily life.

title: 25 · Joining sentences: -고, -지만, -아/어서
blurb: And, but, so. Three endings that turn two short sentences into one natural one.

title: 26 · Telling a story in the past
blurb: String past-tense sentences together with 먼저 · 그리고 · 그다음에 · 그래서 · 마지막으로.

title: 27 · Describing nouns: 좋은 날씨, 큰 가방
blurb: Put an adjective in front of a noun: a big bag, good weather, spicy food.

title: 28 · Comparing: 보다, 더, 제일
blurb: Cheaper than, more, less, the best. Everything you need to compare and choose.

title: 29 · Can't, can, and don't know
blurb: 못 vs 안, -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 / 없어요, and 몰라요 vs 모르겠어요.

title: 30 · Have to: -아/어야 해요
blurb: Say what you must do, ask if you have to, and say when you don't.

title: 31 · Honorific verbs
blurb: -(으)시- and the special verbs: 드시다, 주무시다, 계시다, 말씀하시다.

title: 32 · Asking for things politely
blurb: 좀, 혹시, -아/어 주시겠어요?, -(으)면 안 돼요? — the softeners that get a yes.

title: 33 · Office Korean
blurb: Titles, the 수고 family, email openers and closers, and surviving 회식.
